skill.name: DevOps & Quality
skill.description: Provides concise standards for linting, type checking, version control, CI, testing, and secrets management.
skill.summary: Apply practical DevOps and code-quality standards to a project.
skill.author: AbdulSamad94

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives. The skill uses inline code formatting to name standard tools, configuration files, commit examples, and an environment file; it does not execute commands or access secrets. No prompt injection, data-exfiltration intent, or other semantic security concern was found.

static_findings.snippet: - **Rule**: strict type checking is enabled in `tsconfig.json`.
- **Commit Messages**: Semantic commits preferred (e.g., `feat: add chatbot`, `fix: header overflow`
- **GitHub Actions**: Recommended for running `npm run lint` and `npm run build` on every PR.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format the documented npm lint command as Markdown. This prose does not execute a command or accept input.
The backticks format configuration filenames as Markdown. No shell command or executable code is present.
The backticks format a TypeScript configuration filename as Markdown. The line only states a quality standard.
The backticks mark example commit-message text in documentation. The examples are not commands and cannot execute.
The line recommends standard CI commands in prose, using Markdown code formatting. It supplies no automation or command-execution mechanism.
The backticks format the .env filename as Markdown. The skill does not read, modify, or transmit that file.
The line advises keeping a local .env file out of version control. It contains no secret value and no instruction to expose or access secrets.

content.user_title: Improve DevOps and Code Quality Practices
content.value_statement: Projects often lack consistent checks for quality, delivery, and secret handling. This skill provides a compact baseline for linting, testing, CI, and safe environment configuration.
actual_capabilities: Recommends ESLint linting for code-quality checks.
Calls for strict TypeScript type checking through tsconfig.json.
Describes a feature-branch workflow and semantic commit messages.
Recommends CI checks for linting and builds on pull requests.
Identifies Jest for unit tests and Playwright for end-to-end tests.
Recommends local .env files remain uncommitted and production variables use Vercel.
limitations: Does not create CI workflow files or run commands.
Does not provide project-specific lint or TypeScript configuration.
Does not define test cases, coverage targets, or deployment pipelines.
Assumes Vercel for the stated production environment variable guidance.

use_cases.title: Set a project quality baseline
use_cases.description: Use the standards to define initial linting, typing, testing, and version-control expectations.

use_cases.title: Review pull request checks
use_cases.description: Compare an existing pull request process with the recommended lint, build, unit, and end-to-end checks.

use_cases.title: Document team delivery practices
use_cases.description: Turn the concise guidance into a shared checklist for branches, commits, CI, and secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Start a quality checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple checklist for linting, type checking, tests, and pull request validation in this project.

prompt_templates.title: Plan CI checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on these DevOps standards, propose pull request checks for linting, building, unit tests, and end-to-end tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review secret handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our documented environment-variable process against this skill. List gaps without requesting secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Create an adoption roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this repository against the DevOps and Quality guidance. Prioritize the missing practices by impact and implementation effort.

output_examples.input: Create a pull request quality checklist.
output: Run linting and the production build.
Run unit and end-to-end tests where applicable.
Require a feature branch and a semantic commit message.
Keep local environment files out of version control.

output_examples.input: What should CI run on each pull request?
output_examples.output: Run the lint command and build command first. Add Jest unit tests and Playwright end-to-end tests for relevant changes.

best_practices: Run linting, type checks, and tests before requesting review.
Use feature branches and semantic commit messages for clear history.
Store production secrets in the hosting platform and never commit local environment files.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful build as a substitute for tests.
Adding secrets to source files or committing a local .env file.
Using undocumented branch and commit conventions across a team.

faq.question: Does this skill run linting or tests?
faq.answer: No. It documents recommended tools and practices only.

faq.question: Which linting tool does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends ESLint with the npm run lint command.

faq.question: Does it require a CI provider?
faq.answer: It recommends GitHub Actions, but it does not configure a provider.

faq.question: Which test tools are named?
faq.answer: It names Jest for unit tests and Playwright for end-to-end tests.

faq.question: How should local secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Keep local values in an uncommitted .env file and do not place secrets in source control.

faq.question: Is this a complete deployment guide?
faq.answer: No. It provides high-level quality and CI guidance, not a deployment implementation.
